findings.evidence: Line 493-503: conclusion is `finrank ℂ (ker (gammaMatrix p - m • 1)) = 2`; `f` and `hf` are local `let`/`have` inside the proof.
findings.fix: Either state the docstring as what it proves (two-dimensional, by `injOn_goodProjector` and `exists_apply_eq_zero_and_goodProjector_apply_eq`) and fix the Main-statements bullet to match, or expose the equivalence as a declaration so the claim is backed by a statement.
findings.issue: The docstring of `finrank_ker_gammaMatrix_sub_smul_one` claims "`P₊` maps it isomorphically onto the good spinors", but the statement delivers only `finrank ℂ (ker (gammaMatrix p - m • 1)) = 2`; the `LinearEquiv.ofBijective f hf` is built inside the proof and discarded. The same overclaim is repeated in the module docstring (line 65-67).

findings.evidence: Line 450-452: the conclusion is `∃ ψ, (gammaMatrix p - m • 1) ψ = 0 ∧ L.goodProjector ψ = χ`; the witness `χ + η` appears only at line 472.
findings.fix: Drop the "namely" clause, or promote the witness into the statement (e.g. state the explicit solution rather than an existential).
findings.issue: `exists_apply_eq_zero_and_goodProjector_apply_eq`'s docstring names the witness ("namely of `χ + (2 p⁺)⁻¹ (/p_T + m) γ⁺ χ`"), which is a proof detail, not part of the `∃ ψ, …` statement; it goes stale if the proof changes.

findings.evidence: Lines 170-219 and 305-306 contain `@[simp]`/`theorem` with no preceding `/-- … -/`; contrast lines 160, 165, 213, 217, 294.
findings.fix: Add one-line docstrings stating the identity (`P₊ + P₋ = 1`, `P₊P₋ = 0`, `P₊² = P₊`, …), matching the style already used at lines 160/165/213/294.
findings.issue: Three declarations advertised in "Main statements" have no docstring — `goodProjector_add_badProjector` (171), `goodProjector_mul_badProjector` (191), `goodProjector_mul_self` (202) — as do `goodProjector_def` (142), `badProjector_def` (146), `badProjector_add_goodProjector` (179), `goodProjector_apply_add_badProjector_apply` (183), `badProjector_eq_one_sub` (187), `badProjector_mul_goodProjector` (197), `badProjector_mul_self` (209), `trace_badProjector` (305), while every surrounding lemma (including their bad-side duals elsewhere) is documented.

summary: The module docstring is accurate and genuinely useful, but two docstrings promise an isomorphism/witness the statements do not deliver, and several declarations listed in "Main statements" carry no docstring while all their neighbours do.
